standard_prerequisites.name: Associated points of a Noetherian scheme are finite, and a section of an invertible sheaf not vanishing at any associated point is a regular section whose zero scheme is an effective Cartier divisor, with the corresponding invertible sheaf isomorphic to the structure sheaf twisted by that divisor
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used throughout the proof, at lines 3233-3234, 3240-3242 and 3265-3268
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns a nowhere vanishing condition at finitely many points into regularity and into the description of the invertible sheaf as a divisor class.

standard_prerequisites.name: Existence of a section of a power of an ample invertible sheaf making a prescribed finite set land in an affine open, cited by the author from the properties chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the affine open X_s containing the prescribed points, to which the quasi-affine case is applied.

standard_prerequisites.name: Extendability of sections after multiplication by a power of the defining section, cited by the author from the properties chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the global sections of the twisted invertible sheaves whose zero divisors are the announced D and D'.

core_obligations: Quasi-affine case: with x_1 to x_n the associated points of X, choose a section of the given invertible module that does not vanish at any point of the prescribed finite set or at any associated point, note that it is a regular section by the same-chapter criterion, and conclude that the invertible module is the structure sheaf twisted by the effective Cartier divisor cut out by that section, which by construction avoids the prescribed set (proof lines 3233-3242).

General case, first step: for an ample invertible sheaf choose a positive power and a section of it such that the corresponding open set is affine and contains both the prescribed finite set and the associated points (proof lines 3245-3249).

Restrict and extend: over that affine open apply the quasi-affine case to the given invertible module to get a section avoiding the same finite set, and use the cited extension statement to see that after multiplying by a suitable power of the previous section it extends to a global section of a twist of the module (proof lines 3251-3257).

Conclude: the twisted module and the twist of the structure sheaf by the same power both carry global sections avoiding the prescribed finite set and the associated points, hence are regular and are each the twist by an effective Cartier divisor, so the original invertible module is the difference of the two divisors, both disjoint from the prescribed set (proof lines 3258-3272).
proof_roadmap: Prove the quasi-affine case by choosing a section avoiding the associated points and reading off the divisor class (proof lines 3233-3242).

In general, cover the prescribed points by a principal affine open cut out by a section of a power of an ample sheaf, apply the quasi-affine case there, and extend the section to the whole scheme to obtain the two effective Cartier divisors (proof lines 3243-3272).
difficulty_reason: The lemma realises every invertible module on a Noetherian scheme carrying an ample invertible sheaf as the difference of two effective Cartier divisors, in such a way that a prescribed finite set is avoided, with the quasi-affine case needing only one divisor (statement lines 3215-3230). The counted proof has two genuinely different parts: the quasi-affine case, which chooses a section avoiding the finitely many associated points and converts it into a divisor by the same-chapter criterion for regular sections (proof lines 3233-3242), and the general case, which uses a section of a power of the ample sheaf to isolate an affine open containing the prescribed points, applies the quasi-affine case there, and then extends the section after multiplying by a power of the defining section so that two global regular sections become available (proof lines 3243-3272). It is H2: the argument is complete and uses only standard inputs about associated points, ampleness and extendability of sections, and its content is the assembly of those inputs rather than a research-level construction.
